bib.title: CoQA: A Conversational Question Answering Challenge
bib.venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics (TACL)

read.skipped: References skimmed only; figures (images) not viewed, captions only

question: Can a large conversational reading-comprehension dataset with free-form answers and multiple domains be built, and how well do current dialogue and reading-comprehension models do on it?
hypothesis: Conversational questions (coreference, pragmatics) and free-form answers are not handled by existing span-based reading comprehension models, leaving headroom versus humans.
contributions: CoQA: 127k questions from 8k conversations over passages from seven domains
Analysis of linguistic phenomena in conversational questions
Benchmarks of seq2seq, PGNet, DrQA, augmented DrQA and a combined DrQA+PGNet model

method.summary: Two Amazon Mechanical Turk workers (questioner and answerer) chat about a ~200-word passage; the answerer highlights a rationale span and edits it into a free-form answer. Dev/test get three extra answers per question. Baselines: seq2seq, pointer-generator (PGNet), DrQA, DrQA with yes/no tokens, and DrQA feeding PGNet.
method.task: conversational question answering over a passage

datasets.name: CoQA
datasets.split: In-domain (Children's, Literature, Mid/High School, News, Wikipedia): 100 dev passages and 100 test passages per domain, rest train. Out-of-domain (Reddit, Science): 100 test passages each
datasets.source: Passages from MCTest, Project Gutenberg, RACE, CNN, Wikipedia, Reddit Writing Prompts, AI2 Science Questions; collected on AMT via ParlAI
datasets.preprocessing: Passages with multiple entities/pronominal references chosen with Stanford CoreNLP; truncated to about 200 words; ~12% of conversations had one worker play both roles (train only)

models.name: Seq2seq
models.architecture: 2-layer BiLSTM encoder, LSTM decoder with attention (OpenNMT)
models.context: inferred: passage plus n history turns; n best from Table 9

models.name: DrQA
models.architecture: Document Reader of Chen et al. 2017, LSTM span extractor

models.name: Augmented DrQA
models.architecture: DrQA with yes and no tokens appended to passage

models.name: DrQA+PGNet
models.architecture: DrQA predicts rationale/answer span, PGNet rewrites it into the answer

other.training: DrQA oracle spans fed into PGNet during training

training.lr: seq2seq/PGNet: initial 1.0, decay rate 0.5; DrQA: null
training.dropout: seq2seq/PGNet 0.3 all layers; DrQA 0.4 on LSTM layers, 0.5 on word embeddings

other.drqa_tuning: turns of history, layers, hidden units, dropout tuned on dev
other.gold_span_for_drqa: span with highest F1 to the original answer; rationale used to disambiguate; unknown token if an answer word is absent
other.history: gold previous answers used to predict the next answer

inference.samples: single run per model; no seeds reported
inference.prompting: input format: p <q> q_{i-n} <a> a_{i-n} ... <q> q_{i-1} <a> a_{i-1} <q> q_i

metrics.name: macro-average word-overlap F1
metrics.definition: per question F1 averaged over n=4 human answer sets (original + 3 extra), each set leaving one out for human performance; articles and punctuation removed

eval.protocol: Gold history answers used. Human score: each human answer compared with the other n-1 answers (partitioned into n sets). No significance tests.

limits: F1 word overlap is an imperfect metric for free-form answers; the authors say a better metric is beyond scope (Sec 6.3)
Human agreement lowest on unanswerable questions and non-overlapping answers
Questioner sees the passage so question independence from passage is incomplete
Gold previous answers are used as history in evaluation, not model predictions
Baselines are pre-BERT; paper notes BERT-based systems reached 82.8 F1 by Jan 2019, so the 65.4 numbers have dated
Reddit and Science out-of-domain only 100 passages each (about 1.5-1.7k Q/A)
No seeds, batch size, epochs or compute reported for the baselines

terms.definition: a contiguous text span in the passage highlighted by the answerer as evidence; not provided at test time
